entry.title: Your data has layers, most data teams see only one
entry.content:
Your data has layers, most data teams see only one

 

The Terminology Problem

"Master data," "semantics," and "context" appear in almost every data architecture and governance conversation. They show up in vendor pitches, platform documentation, and cross-functional design sessions, often used interchangeably and rarely defined with any precision. For a data steward, analyst, or engineer trying to build something that actually works, that imprecision has real consequences. SAP has specific, deliberate definitions for each of these terms, and those definitions connect directly to how its data solutions are built and how they fit together. Getting precise about the language is not a mere naming exercise. It is the difference between an architecture that holds and one that quietly fails at the seams.

The three layers of data: what they are and what each one addresses

Master Data: The Foundation

SAP defines master data as the core business entities that give your processes their meaning and continuity: customers, suppliers, products, materials, employees, locations, etc. These are the nouns of your business. They do not change with every transaction, but everything important depends on them being accurate, consistent, and trusted across every system that touches them.

In the SAP portfolio, two solutions address master data from different angles. SAP Master Data Governance (MDG) governs master data at the SAP core, enforcing policies, managing change request workflows, and maintaining data stewardship inside core business processes. SAP Reltio approaches it from the enterprise perspective. It takes records from SAP, Salesforce, Oracle, legacy ERPs, and any other system in your landscape, identifies which records represent the same real-world entity, and produces a unified, trusted consolidated profile available to every downstream system, analytical tool, and AI agent.

In an Order to Cash process, when a sales order comes in for Acme Corp, the master data is the foundation: the customer record carrying the name, billing address, payment terms, preferred delivery method, and credit limit. SAP MDG ensures that record was created and maintained correctly inside SAP. SAP Reltio ensures that the Acme Corp record sitting in your CRM and used in the Order to Cash business process is recognized as the same, trusted entity used in downstream analytics and AI, not a duplicate or a shadow record living a separate life in a parallel system.

Semantics: The Meaning Layer

Master data tells you what your entities are. Semantics tells you what they mean.

SAP defines semantics as the business meaning assigned to data: the definitions, relationships, and rules that transform a technical data structure into something a business process can understand and act on. A field named "KUNNR" in SAP S/4HANA means nothing to a data scientist pulling it into a model. A semantically enriched version of that same field tells a different story. It is labeled "Customer Number," typed as an identifier, linked to the Customer entity, and given valid value ranges. That version is immediately useful.

This is the space that SAP Datasphere, the data integration and management layer within SAP Business Data Cloud (BDC), is designed for. The semantic layer in SAP Datasphere lets data teams define what data means in business terms, independent of the underlying technical structure. You model entities, attributes, and relationships at the business level, and that semantic model becomes the common language between your source systems and every analytical or operational consumer downstream.

Back in the Order to Cash scenario: Acme Corp's master record has a credit limit field. Semantics define what that field means in practice. It represents the maximum outstanding balance in USD before new orders are blocked, it is linked to the credit exposure calculation, and it triggers a specific pricing tier. Without that semantic layer, a data analyst pulling credit data from three different systems has no reliable way of knowing whether she is comparing the same thing.

Context: The Situational Layer

Semantics tells you what your data means in general. Context tells you what it means right now, in this process, for this decision.

SAP defines context as the situational information that gives data its relevance: the process it is embedded in, the time it was captured, the relationships it holds to other data points at a specific moment. Context is what transforms a well-defined, semantically accurate data asset into something you can act on.

SAP Business Data Cloud addresses context at an architectural level. By integrating master data, transactional data, analytical data, and operational metadata inside a curated data product, SAP BDC allows every piece of data to be understood in relation to the business processes around it. Not as an isolated record, but as part of a live operational picture.

In the Order to Cash scenario, context is what tells you that Acme Corp currently has $85,000 of their $100,000 credit limit utilized, that two invoices are overdue, that their contract was renewed last week, and that the sales rep submitted a priority flag on the account this morning. The master data has not changed. The semantic definitions have not changed. But the context is different from last month, and it should change how this order is handled.

This is the transactional layer of context: the live operational state that gives data its situational relevance. The broader business context layer goes further, encoding process intelligence, institutional memory, unstructured document knowledge, and AI governance constraints. Together, those elements form a complete picture of how an enterprise operates and what its AI agents are permitted to do. That conversation deserves its own post (and it is available here, Why Your AI Strategy Needs a Robust Business Context).

How the Three Layers Connect

These three terms describe three distinct layers of a complete data architecture, and each one depends on the one beneath it.

Master data is the what: the trusted entities your business runs on. Semantics is the meaning: the definitions and relationships that make those entities interpretable across systems and teams. Context is the relevance: the situational lens that makes data actionable in a specific moment and process.

When one layer is missing or broken, the layers above it fail. Imprecise master data produces semantically rich models of unreliable entities. Clear semantics over untrustworthy master data gives you well-labeled friction. And accurate master data with solid semantics but no contextual layer leaves your AI agents and analytics tools making decisions without the situational intelligence they need to get it right.

SAP MDG and SAP Reltio address the master data layer, governance at the SAP core and unification across the enterprise. SAP Datasphere addresses the semantics layer, translating technical structures into business-meaningful models. SAP Business Data Cloud addresses context, connecting the data layers into a unified architecture where everything is understood in relation to everything else.

For the data professional building or operating within this stack, the practical takeaway is straightforward: the quality of your outputs, whether that is an analytics dashboard, an AI-generated recommendation, or an automated process decision, depends on how well all three layers are working. Not just one of them.

Where This Gets Real

I have watched teams spend months on semantic modeling while their master data was still fragmented across five systems. The layers look independent on a diagram, but they are not in practice. If you are working through this in your own environment, I would genuinely like to hear where the friction is. Drop a comment below or follow along. This is a conversation worth having.

entry.title: What AI-Native, Autonomous Master Data Looks Like in SAP Business Data Cloud
entry.content:
The MDM Renaissance: What AI-Native, Autonomous Master Data Looks Like in SAP Business Data Cloud

In the last blog, The MDM gap just got closed: What SAP Reltio in SAP Business Data Cloud means for your data, we talked about architecture. Why SAP Reltio fills the unification gap that SAP Master Data Governance (MDG) was never designed to address. Why do two complementary products inside SAP Business Data Cloud (BDC) make more sense than asking one to do both jobs. If that framing landed for you, good, because this piece is about what comes next.

Master Data Management (MDM) is having a moment. Not in the "press release" sense, but in the "this actually matters for AI" sense. For years, master data management was something organizations did because they had to. The projects were driven by compliance mandates, not business appetite. They ran long, cost more than anyone budgeted, and delivered less than the slide decks promised. Governance got tacked on as a control layer, which meant it landed in people's laps as overhead rather than value, and left a lot of data professionals with a complicated relationship with the whole discipline. Then AI arrived and moved the urgency from "someday" to "right now."

The good news is that SAP has been building toward this, and the roadmap for SAP MDG and SAP Reltio together in SAP BDC gives data professionals something genuinely worth paying attention to.

Master data as a data product: the bigger idea behind entity resolution

When people ask what SAP Reltio is doing inside SAP BDC, the answer they get often starts and ends with "entity resolution." That is accurate but incomplete. The bigger idea is what happens after entity resolution.

The principle is straightforward. Master data sits across your landscape, in SAP applications, in Salesforce, in an Oracle or JD Edwards instance still running core processes, or in that legacy system you just cannot seem to get off of. SAP MDG governs creation and validation at the SAP core. SAP Reltio pulls from all of it, resolves the duplicates, and consolidates across domains. What you end up with is something that belongs at the center of your data strategy: a trusted master data record that the rest of the business can rely on.

This is where SAP BDC's data products concept becomes directly relevant to MDM. Fabian Hartje, who heads product management for MDM in SAP BDC, described it this way: "whatever we do inside of this layer of master data management is exposing Unified Data Products. And these Unified Data Products that are being exposed from master data management are some special types of data products." Special because they consolidate across sources. Special because they reflect what the business knows, not what one system believes.

Data products in SAP BDC are a shared, governed, reusable asset. That principle extends to master data. The clean consolidated record that SAP MDG and SAP Reltio together produce is not a siloed output for the MDM team to manage in isolation. It becomes available to the broader SAP BDC ecosystem. You can consume it in SAP Analytics Cloud. You can power business applications built on You can expose it through SAP BDC Connect to Databricks, Snowflake, or other supported platforms where data engineers are working. The record that used to live in the MDM silo becomes a shared resource for everyone downstream, including SAP Joule and your AI agents.

AI-native is not a feature. It is a design philosophy.

SAP Reltio describes itself as AI-native. If you have spent any time watching AI capabilities, get bolted onto existing products, you know the difference that design philosophy makes in practice.

Here is what AI-native looks like concretely for a data steward. The moment data is loaded; AI applies to the matching process. The platform looks for records that represent the same real-world entity across different sources and flags them for unification. That already reduces the volume of manual review dramatically. Then agents run enrichment workflows, pulling third-party data to fill gaps and running records back through matching to see if the enriched version now resolves additional duplicates. Then a decision agent handles the match cases that have a clear answer, so the human steward only sees the genuinely ambiguous ones.

Mike Frasca, VP of Product Management for SAP Reltio, described the outcome simply: "Their workload becomes significantly smaller and focused on the things that are really important.  The really really tough questions.” That is a meaningful shift. Instead of four hours of yes/yes/no/yes decisions, stewards spend their time on the cases that actually require judgment. The rest runs.

There is another dimension to AI-native that often gets overlooked: delivery speed. SAP Reltio is built API-first, designed for real-time operational use cases from day one. That matters because the way most organizations have experienced MDM historically is batch-based. Data gets processed, cleaned, and made available hours or days later. That model does not work when the consumer is an AI agent that needs to act now. Not batch MDM feeding analytics two days later. Data delivered at the speed AI needs it.

What is coming next on the AI front for SAP Reltio is moving AI directly into tenant configuration and operations. Making it easier to set up new entity types, making data loads smarter, reducing the implementation friction that has historically made MDM projects feel expensive and slow.

SAP Master Data Governance is heading somewhere interesting too

When you hear "autonomous MDM," it probably sounds like a future-state aspiration. For SAP MDG, it is an active design direction.

The traditional governance workflow looks like this: data enters a workflow, a local tax manager reviews it, a regional data owner approves it, it moves forward. Every step is human-configured and human-executed. It works. It is also slow, and the reasons humans are in those approval steps are actually expressible as policies.

The question the SAP MDG team is exploring is: what if an agent could be trained on those policies and handle the review steps that have a deterministic right answer? What if human intervention became the exception rather than the default state of every workflow?

Rene Kirchoff, Head of Product Management for SAP MDG, framed it this way: "an agent-led operating model, with human supervision and exception management." That is not autonomous in the sense of removing humans from the loop entirely. It is autonomous in the sense that the loop runs without humans unless something unusual happens.

The near-term version of this is already in motion. SAP Joule is being used to enable business users, not just application experts, to work with master data directly in SAP MDG. The longer-term direction is governance that runs itself, with humans stepping in when a situation genuinely warrants it.

The practical integration picture

If you are an existing SAP MDG customer, or you are advising one, the question is probably not whether this direction is interesting. It is what it looks like in your landscape.

SAP Reltio is now commercially available as part of SAP BDC, provisioned the same way you would provision any other SAP BDC component. Customers can allocate SAP BDC capacity units across SAP MDG and SAP Reltio depending on their use cases. You do not have to choose one or the other; the architecture is designed for both.

SAP MDG is also being integrated into SAP BDC's underlying infrastructure through UCL (Unified Customer Layer) and formation management, with full data product exposure by end of year. Whatever SAP MDG produces, clean governed master data from the SAP core, becomes part of the same data product fabric that SAP Reltio and every other SAP BDC component draws from.

The division of responsibility is intentional and worth being explicit about. SAP MDG's job is to get data right at the point it enters your SAP systems. It enforces the policies, drives validation workflows, and ensures that what gets created in your ERP meets your standards from day one. That governed record is the foundation everything downstream depends on.

SAP Reltio's job is what happens across the full enterprise. A supplier that appears in your ERP, your procurement platform, and a system inherited from an acquisition is three separate records until SAP Reltio reconciles them. That reconciliation, built into a continuously maintained 360-degree view across all your master data domains, customers, suppliers, materials, assets, is what SAP Reltio delivers. Together, the two give you governance at the point of creation and a trusted, consolidated view across everything that already exists in your landscape.

One more dimension worth naming: scale. A Fortune 500 organization is not dealing with a few million customer records. It is dealing with billions, across customers, suppliers, products, and transactions. SAP Reltio is already operating at that level today. And because SAP's existing footprint covers so much of that landscape already, extending it with non-SAP data does not mean rebuilding from scratch. It means expanding something that is already running. That also extends horizontally: as agentic capabilities reduce the cost of onboarding new domains, governance can expand beyond the traditional core objects, customer, supplier, product, to any data that matters to the business.  This is not “nice-to-have,” but a necessity to manage your data at scale beyond the typical domains to enable the full potential of the Autonomous Enterprise.

MDM inside the knowledge core: why this is bigger than a data quality story

SAP BDC is built around a concept called the knowledge core. It is where business semantics, knowledge graphs, canonical models, and governed data products come together into a shared system of understanding. The idea is that context should be maintained continuously and applied consistently, not reconstructed from scratch for every AI use case or business function.

Consider what happens without it. You deploy AI agents across your business. Procurement optimizes for cost. Finance optimizes for cash flow. Compliance manages for risk. Each decision is locally rational. But if those agents are not reasoning from the same shared context about priorities, constraints, and relationships, their decisions start to conflict. Speed decreases. Alignment breaks down.

The knowledge core addresses this by grounding every agent in a shared understanding of the business. And here is where master data becomes strategic, not just operational.

Master data represents the entities that everything else in the business connects to. Customers, suppliers, materials, employees. Every knowledge graph node, every semantic definition, every data product that flows through SAP BDC ultimately points back to one of these entities. If those entities are fragmented, duplicated, or inconsistently defined across systems, the knowledge core has a structural problem at its foundation. The graph has conflicting nodes for the same real-world entity. The semantics do not align. The context agents receive is not actually shared.

This is the MDM problem, expressed at an AI scale.

SAP MDG and SAP Reltio address it from two directions. SAP MDG governs the data at the SAP core (leveraging the SAP S/4HANA canonical model), ensuring that the entities entering your systems are clean, validated, and policy-compliant from day one. SAP Reltio reconciles the entity layer across the enterprise, resolving the fragmentation that exists in every landscape that has grown organically over time. Together they give the knowledge core what it needs to function: a single, trusted, continuously maintained understanding of who your customers are, who your suppliers are, and what your materials actually are, across every system and every function.

That is what analysts are beginning to call converged data management platforms (CDMPs) or modern data and AI platforms, the move from individual tools solving individual problems toward a single, open platform where data management, semantics, and AI reasoning are connected rather than siloed. SAP BDC is built on that model. And MDM, governed and unified, is what makes the entity layer of that platform coherent.

Why MDM got exciting again

There was a period, roughly the five to eight years before AI took over every technology conversation, where master data management was not exactly a headline topic. It was necessary work that organizations did because they had to, and it sat quietly in the background.

What has changed is the stakes. An AI agent running a billing workflow, processing a supplier invoice, or answering a question from a sales team does not pause to check whether its underlying data is reliable. It acts on what it has. If what it has is fragmented, duplicated, or stale, it acts wrongly, at speed, at scale.

That dynamic is what has brought MDM back to the front of the conversation, and what makes the SAP investment in this space significant. Not just acquiring a technology, but building a coherent architecture where governed master data at the SAP core, unified master data across the enterprise, and data quality at scale all operate as a single capability layer inside SAP BDC.

The three pillars are simple to remember: govern at source, unify across the enterprise, ensure data quality at scale. SAP MDG handles the first. SAP Reltio handles the second and third. Together they produce the kind of trusted, consistent master data that analytics, AI agents, and SAP Joule can actually depend on.

Three years from now, the expectation inside the product teams is that MDM looks fundamentally different. Configuration is AI-assisted. Governance runs on agents with human exception handling. Data stewards focus on the decisions that require real judgment. And the clean, trusted master data that all of that produces becomes the default context for every AI-driven process in the business.

That is not a projection. That is the direction the product teams are actively building toward. And if you are working on data quality, data governance, or master data today, it is worth understanding what the architecture they are assembling actually enables.

To learn more about SAP Reltio, SAP Master Data Governance, and the full MDM portfolio in SAP Business Data Cloud, visit sap.com/products/data-cloud/master-data-management.

entry.title: The Evolution of SAP Master Data Governance with SAP Business Data Cloud
entry.content:
The Inflection Point

SAP's master data management strategy has reached an inflection point. With SAP Business Data Cloud (BDC) as the trusted data foundation for the Business AI Platform, SAP is reflecting its master data management (MDM) capabilities within two complementary solutions: SAP Master Data Governance (MDG) for central governance at the SAP source, and SAP Reltio for enterprise-wide data unification. As part of this realignment, SAP is discontinuing the SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP)-based SAP Master Data Governance, cloud edition.

Two Complementary MDM solutions in SAP Business Data Cloud

SAP Master Data Governance provides central governance at the point of creation - enforcing workflows, validations, approval, and compliance standards with deep SAP S/4HANA integration. SAP MDG is the system of record for operational master data in the SAP landscape.

SAP Reltio addresses data unification from the decentral perspective: consolidating records from diverse sources - SAP and non-SAP - resolving duplicates and delivering a consistent 360-degree view across domains as a unified data product. Reltio operates in real time, at scale, and is the system of context for enterprise-wide master data.

Together, they form a complete MDM architecture inside SAP BDC. Use SAP MDG when governance at the SAP source is the priority. Use SAP Reltio when unification and cross-system data quality are the priority. Use both when the goal is governed creation plus enterprise-wide unification.

 

Discontinuation of SAP Master Data Governance, Cloud Edition

With SAP Reltio comprehensively covering data unification and non-SAP use cases, and with SAP MDG's well established Governance capabilities, SAP has decided to discontinue the SAP BTP-based SAP Master Data Governance, cloud edition.

  • Existing subscriptions will be honored through contract end. Renewals will not be possible.
  • The Free Tier offering is not available anymore.
  • The SAP BTP-based offering will be phased out of BTPEA/CPEA/PayGo along SAP standard procedures.
  • For details, contact your SAP Account Executive.

Focus on Central Governance

SAP MDG is a core component of SAP Business Data Cloud with a strengthened focus on governance for SAP Cloud ERP. SAP Reltio does not replace SAP MDG - it extends your MDM footprint beyond the SAP landscape. This is a use case decision: use each solution at a position where it plays to its strengths.

For SAP S/4HANA-related master data governance, use SAP MDG in SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Private Edition for private cloud deployment and SAP MDG in SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Public Edition public cloud deployment. Visit the community topic page and follow the tag SAP Master Data Governance to stay up-to-date.

For more on SAP's MDM strategy, also read What SAP Reltio in SAP Business Data Cloud means for your data?

entry.title: Working with SAP Business Data Cloud in the SAP Business AI Platform: The Data Engineer Perspective
entry.content:
Assistants and agents are becoming regular consumers of the data products you build. They support decisions and execute multi-step tasks across SAP and third-party systems, and unlike human analysts, they treat what they receive as business truth. A stale metric that a planner might question could be used by an AI agent as fact, turning a data quality issue into a flawed recommendation or automated action. For data engineers, the requirement is clear: data products must be current, complete, semantically correct, and authorized.

SAP Business AI Platform brings together the capabilities needed to build, run, and govern AI, including the business data and context used to ground it. Within this platform, SAP Business Data Cloud (SAP BDC) provides the governed data foundation and shared business semantics, while SAP Knowledge Graph adds relationships and process context. For data engineers, the focus is on keeping this foundation reliable from source to consumption: connecting systems, orchestrating data flows, preserving business context, monitoring freshness and quality, handling change and failure, maintaining traceability, and enabling governed access across platforms.

 

What stays the same

The fundamentals of data engineering remain. You still design, build, and operate pipelines that connect source systems with the environments where data is governed, processed, and consumed across SAP and non-SAP landscapes. The work still involves large data volumes, complex dependencies, transformations, changing schemas, and workloads that must remain dependable as source systems evolve.

You also continue to work closely with data modelers and data stewards. Modelers define structures, relationships, calculations, and business entities. Stewards establish ownership, quality expectations, certification, and governance requirements. Data engineers operationalize those decisions by implementing pipelines, preserving semantics through transformations, enforcing technical controls, and keeping products reliable in production. The core responsibility is unchanged: make trusted business data available where and when it is needed.

SAP BDC strengthens this work with integration, orchestration, governed sharing, semantics, lineage, and monitoring capabilities across SAP and non-SAP landscapes. A business data fabric does not eliminate the need for engineering discipline. It gives pipelines, data products, semantics, lineage, and sharing a common purpose: making business data usable across analytics, planning, applications, and AI without rebuilding context for every consumer.

 

What changes in practice

The first change is the consumer. AI assistants and agents become first-class consumers of data products alongside analysts, applications, planning tools, and data science workloads, and they consume data differently from experienced human users. A planner may recognize that an inventory figure looks stale or know that a status code has an undocumented exception. An agent cannot be expected to have that knowledge. The data product must expose freshness, meaning, relationships, quality, and access explicitly.

The second change is the unit of delivery. Instead of building datasets and pipelines for individual use cases, data engineers increasingly deliver governed, reusable data products. SAP-managed data products provide ready-to-use SAP application data with business context, reducing the need to build and maintain pipelines that extract and reconstruct this data from source systems. This allows data engineers to focus more on creating derived data products - combining, transforming, and enriching SAP and non-SAP data for organization-specific needs.

The third change is operations. AI-ready data engineering moves away from “batch and forget” toward controlled orchestration and continuous visibility into freshness, volume, schema drift, dependencies, failures, and quality thresholds. A successful job execution is not enough. The resulting product must remain discoverable, explainable, governed, observable, and dependable for both people and AI. That means engineering for failure as deliberately as for success: retries, recovery, dependency management, alerts, reconciliation, lineage, and clear signals when a data product can no longer be trusted downstream.

Whatever the consumption pattern, the requirement is the same: reliable AI depends on reliable data products.

 

How AI-ready data engineering works with SAP BDC

Think of AI-ready data engineering as a productized data supply chain. Operational systems provide business facts. Pipelines ingest, replicate, transform, harmonize, and prepare them. Master data and semantic models establish consistent meaning. Catalog and lineage make the resulting products discoverable and traceable. Governed access makes them reusable across platforms. The shift is not only from source to target, but from data movement to governed context, which SAP Business AI Platform can consume so assistants and agents can support decisions and execute approved steps.

Consider supply planning. A change in demand may affect procurement, manufacturing, inventory, and logistics. The engineering challenge is not to copy a demand table from one system to another; it is to assemble and operate a dependable product that provides current context across the process. You might combine SAP-managed product, supplier, inventory, and demand data with logistics signals from a third-party environment through SAP Datasphere and governed zero-copy access, with master data keeping materials, suppliers, customers, and partners consistent. You then make that product operational: orchestrating dependencies, preserving semantics through transformations, monitoring freshness and quality, exposing lineage, enforcing access, and designing recovery for when a source or step fails. The same product can then support a demand-risk model, an AI agent, and a planner in SAP Analytics Cloud without a separate pipeline or separate interpretation for each.

The goal is not to engineer “for AI” as a separate data stack. It is to engineer reusable business data products reliable enough to serve analytics, applications, planning, models, assistants, and agents through the same governed foundation. That foundation is stronger when the architecture is explicit: layers, product types, transformation rules, and reusable blueprints give both human teams and AI-assisted delivery clear guardrails.

This also changes the multi-cloud question. With SAP Business Data Cloud Connect and zero-copy patterns, data does not need to be copied into every environment where processing or AI takes place. The engineering question is no longer only “How do I make this data available?” but also “Does this data need to be copied, or can it be governed and consumed where it already lives?”

 

Impact on trust and operations

In an Autonomous Enterprise, trust depends directly on operations. If an agent recommends a procurement action, triggers a workflow, or supports an exception decision, teams may need to know which data product informed it, where that data originated, how it was transformed, how current it was, whether it passed quality checks, and whether the consumer was authorized to use it. The pipeline is the first link in that accountability chain.

A pipeline can be technically running while its output is operationally unsafe: a source may have stopped updating, a schema change may have altered a transformation, a dependency may have completed with incomplete records, or a replicated table may be available but outside its freshness target. AI-ready engineering means monitoring the state of the data product, not only the state of the job.

Lineage is equally practical. If an AI output references “net revenue by region,” that metric should resolve to the same governed definition used by reporting and analytics, not to an undocumented parallel calculation. Teams need to trace the path from source through transformation to the product consumed downstream and identify where a problem entered it. The same applies to recovery: when something fails, the design should make it possible to identify affected products and consumers, restore processing safely, reconcile the data, and determine when the product can again be treated as trustworthy.

Side channels, ad hoc scripts, and unregistered staging areas make all of this harder. If a data flow is invisible to catalog, lineage, monitoring, and governance, it becomes harder to establish whether an AI agent should depend on it. For AI-ready data products, operational reliability and trust are two sides of the same engineering problem.

 

How this maps to SAP BDC components

SAP BDC brings together capabilities that address different parts of the data engineering lifecycle, with SAP-managed data products as the starting point.

  • SAP-managed data products provide governed SAP application data with business semantics already preserved, reducing the need for data engineers to build and maintain pipelines that extract and reconstruct the same data from source systems. Engineers can consume these products directly or use them as the foundation for derived data products that combine, transform, and enrich SAP and non-SAP data.
  • SAP Datasphere supports integration, modeling, and sharing across the business data fabric. Data engineers can connect SAP and non-SAP data, create derived data products, and use catalog and lineage capabilities to make them discoverable and traceable.
  • SAP BW allows existing BW data and business logic to participate in SAP BDC as data products while retaining established business meaning, reducing the need to reconstruct proven logic in new pipelines.
  • SAP HANA Cloud supports real-time processing, transformations, calculation views, application-facing data, and retrieval patterns such as vector search.
  • SAP Databricks and SAP Snowflake extend SAP BDC with governed data engineering, analytics, data warehousing, and AI/ML capabilities across data lakehouse and warehouse architectures.
  • SAP Master Data Governance and SAP Reltio support consistent master data across SAP and non-SAP landscapes, so data products and pipelines operate on harmonized business entities.
  • SAP Business Data Cloud Connect enables governed sharing and zero-copy access to data products across SAP Databricks, SAP Snowflake, and supported third-party platforms, allowing data to be used where processing occurs without unnecessary replication.
  • SAP Knowledge Graph connects governed data products and their business semantics through relationships and process context, providing richer context for AI reasoning.
  • SAP Business AI Platform uses this governed data and business context to build, run, and govern AI applications and agents.
  • Joule Studio supports custom agents and skills and will become the home of the data product creation agent, bringing AI-assisted data product development into the engineering workflow.
  • SAP Integration Suite connects agents to approved APIs, events, and workflows when AI reasoning needs to translate into actions across systems.

The value is not that every workload moves into one technology. SAP-managed data products provide a governed starting point, so data engineers do not have to rebuild pipelines and business context that SAP already provides. They can focus instead on integrating additional data, creating derived data products, and operating those products reliably across platforms. This requires clear responsibility for ingestion, transformation, semantics, orchestration, sharing, monitoring, lineage, and consumption across the architecture.

 

Where data engineers should focus next

Preparing for AI does not require data engineers to learn an entirely new discipline. It requires applying familiar engineering practices to governed data products that may now be consumed by analysts, applications, assistants, and agents.

  • Build on governed data products and minimize data replication. Reuse SAP-managed or organization-specific data products when they already expose the required business data, semantics, and governance. Create derived data products only when additional transformation, enrichment, or reusable logic is needed. Prefer zero-copy access, federation, and virtualized consumption where technically appropriate, and introduce physical replication only when required for performance, resilience, or workload isolation.
  • Engineer for data reliability, not just pipeline success. Define measurable expectations for freshness, completeness, accuracy, and availability, and monitor them at the data-product level. Design explicitly for source outages, schema evolution, dependency failures, late or missing data, reconciliation, replay, and recovery. A successful pipeline run does not guarantee that the resulting data product is current, complete, correct, or ready for consumption.
  • Preserve business semantics and end-to-end traceability. When transforming, enriching, or combining data, retain the business meaning required to interpret it, including calculation logic, units, currencies, relationships, keys, and hierarchies. Use the lineage capabilities available in SAP BDC to trace data from source through transformation to downstream products and consumers. Where end-to-end lineage cannot be captured automatically, document the missing lineage so that dependencies and traceability gaps are clear.
  • Control how data is consumed by AI. Assistants and agents should access data through the same authorization, governance, and policy controls as other consumers. Expose sufficient metadata and operational signals for AI consumers to determine whether a data product is fresh, complete, reliable, and appropriate for the intended use. AI systems should not treat a data product as current business truth when its operational state cannot be established.

Above all, engineer and operate for the state of the data product, not merely the state of the pipeline. Pipeline execution is an implementation detail. What matters to consumers is whether the resulting data is trustworthy and fit for use. For AI workloads in particular, freshness, quality, lineage, and operational reliability are integral to trustworthy business context.

 

The takeaway

SAP Business AI Platform does not replace data engineering with AI. It increases the importance of good data engineering. Pipelines no longer support only reports, dashboards, and applications. They shape what assistants and agents know, how current that knowledge is, which business meaning applies, and whether an AI-supported action can be traced back to governed and authorized data.

SAP BDC provides the governed data foundation, managed data products, and platform capabilities. Data engineers make that foundation operational by integrating additional sources, creating derived data products, orchestrating data flows, handling scale and change, monitoring freshness and quality, maintaining traceability, engineering recovery, and making governed data products dependable enough to be reused across analytics and AI. In the Autonomous Enterprise, that reliability is part of what makes AI-supported execution possible.

What are you seeing in your own SAP BDC projects? Are your pipelines and data products ready to support AI assistants and agents, or are freshness, observability, lineage, and recovery still evolving? Join the Data Professionals community to discuss engineering patterns and share how you are using SAP BDC as a foundation for the Autonomous Enterprise.

 

How data engineers fit into the BDC data team

This blog is part of a series that explores how the SAP Business AI Platform (BAIP) impacts day‑to‑day work across key data professional roles.

Each role in this series contributes a different part of the trusted business context that analytics, applications, assistants, and agents need. The relationship between the data engineer, data modeler, and data steward is particularly close: modelers define the semantic structures that give a product meaning, stewards establish ownership, certification, and quality expectations, and data engineers turn those definitions into running systems through ingestion, transformation, orchestration, monitoring, lineage, access, and recovery. Data analysts validate and consume insights, data scientists develop and evaluate models, AI engineers build retrieval patterns and agents, and enterprise architects set landscape guardrails. The data engineer is the operational backbone, turning governed business context into reliable, current, scalable, resilient, and production-ready data products.

entry.title: SAP TechEd 2026: Must-Attend Sessions for Data Professionals
entry.content:
SAP TechEd 2026 (October 27–29) offers no shortage of sessions on data, AI, architecture, and analytics. The harder question is which ones deserve a place on your agenda. With SAP Business Data Cloud now in production and AI capabilities expanding across the SAP portfolio, this year’s most valuable sessions should help you, the practitioner, move beyond product updates to make better decisions about what to build, govern, modernize, and scale.

This blog narrows the field to the sessions I believe are most relevant for five data and AI practitioner personas: Enterprise Architects, Data Stewards, Data Engineers, Data Analysts, and Data Scientists. The selections emphasize practical takeaways, from designing governed data foundations and modernizing pipelines to enabling trusted, context-rich AI, so you can focus on the sessions most likely to inform your next project.

Whether attending in-person or virtual start building your agenda now — choose the sessions that match your role and share your must-attend picks with peers in the Data and AI Professionals community to keep the conversation and practical learning going well beyond the event.

This list reflects my own picks, so I've likely missed a few gems. If there's a session you're planning to attend that didn't make the cut, drop it in the comments — I'd love to know what's on your radar.

 

Keynotes

KEY100 | Built for the ones who build

KEY100V | Built for the ones who build (virtual)

Why Attend

SAP TechEd's opening keynote answers the question every architect and practitioner is asking: what can I actually build on SAP's AI platform today? SAP unifies AI, business data, governance, agents, and a new UX layer into one integrated platform — eliminating manual data pipelines, model training overhead, and unpredictable AI costs. Hear directly from SAP leadership what is production-ready now and leave with a clear picture of the business outcomes you can start delivering immediately.

Key Takeaways

  • SAP Business AI Platform unifies AI, data, governance, agents, and UX into one platform — eliminating manual pipeline setup, training overhead, and unpredictable infrastructure costs.
  • Designed so developers, architects, and practitioners focus on building outcomes, not managing underlying complexity.
  • For IT leaders evaluating adoption timelines, this session defines what is production-ready now versus what is on the horizon.

 

KEY101 | Agent v0.0.7 - A license to skill

KEY101V | Agent v0.0.7 - A license to skill (virtual)

Why Attend

Master the AI-driven development revolution. Join Agent Kasimir to see how SAP Business AI Platform, Joule Studio, and open ecosystem tools empower practitioners in AI-driven development. The session shows data professionals how agentic orchestration and context-aware AI work together — redefining how enterprise solutions are built across SAP and non-SAP environments. Evaluating how AI agents fit your analytics workflows? This session moves you from concept to action.

Key Takeaways

  • Joule Studio gives practitioners a supported entry point to build and orchestrate enterprise-grounded AI agents — without starting from scratch.
  • Data professionals get a path to AI workflows where agents reason over business data, coordinate, and integrate across SAP and non-SAP tools.
  • SAP's agentic AI is built on openness — ecosystem tools sit first-class alongside SAP-native capabilities, amplifying existing investments, not displacing them.

 

Enterprise Architects

ST135 | Agent interoperability: Protocols, patterns, and enterprise strategy

Why Attend

As multi-agent AI reaches enterprise scale, interoperability becomes an architectural imperative — this strategy session delivers the protocol-level knowledge architects and developers need. It covers open standards and integration patterns, including A2A and MCP, enabling secure, composable agent networks across SAP and third-party platforms. Leave with the foundation for enterprise-scale AI architectures designed to interoperate — not just orchestrate.

Key Takeaways

  • Agent2Agent (A2A) defines how AI agents from different vendors communicate — the foundational protocol for multi-agent networks spanning SAP and third-party systems.
  • MCP governs agent access to enterprise tools and APIs — mastering A2A and MCP together is essential for reliable cross-platform architectures at enterprise scale.
  • The session delivers practical patterns for building secure, composable agent networks across SAP and non-SAP — a blueprint for expanding agent ecosystems confidently.

 

XP113 | Build AI agents on SAP and non-SAP data and context in an open lakehouse

Why Attend

If your organization is evaluating SAP Business Data Cloud with Dremio, this is the technical blueprint for building AI agents that reason across your full data estate without siloed or ungoverned copies. The session shows how architects and developers use Apache Iceberg and Apache Polaris to integrate SAP and third-party data in an open lakehouse — creating governed data products and ontologies that power Joule agents and enable external consumption through A2A. You'll leave with a clear, end-to-end path from unified data to production-ready agentic AI.

Key Takeaways

  • An open lakehouse on Apache Iceberg and Apache Polaris unifies SAP and third-party data into a single governed layer — giving AI agents real-time access to the full data estate without movement, duplication, or governance compromise.
  • Zero-copy access ensures AI agents always reason over current, authoritative data — reducing management overhead while keeping security and compliance controls intact.
  • A2A protocols extend governed data products beyond SAP boundaries — giving architects a composable foundation where Joule and third-party agents access business context through standardized, controlled interfaces.

 

RA110 | Joule and SAP Knowledge Graph: Context-aware AI across SAP solutions

RA110V | Joule and SAP Knowledge Graph: Context-aware AI across SAP solutions (virtual)

Why Attend

Context separates a generically intelligent AI from one that truly understands your business — this session reveals how SAP AI Core, the orchestration layer behind Joule, delivers that context at scale. You’ll learn how to extend Joule Agents, leverage the Joule Studio model library, connect SAP Business Data Cloud data products, and embed AI directly in SAP S/4HANA. For professionals designing AI agent architectures or SAP analytics integrations, this is where governance, context, and intelligence converge in a production-ready architecture.

Key Takeaways

  • SAP AI Core is the orchestration layer that governs how Joule agents access models, coordinate reasoning, and embed AI directly into SAP S/4HANA within a fully auditable architecture.
  • Joule agents ground every action in trusted data via SAP Business Data Cloud and AI Core, while SAP Knowledge Graph anchors reasoning in real business relationships — delivering business-aware decisions, not generic predictions.
  • The result is an AI architecture where context, governance, and intelligence are built in by design — giving architects a production-ready foundation for extending Joule across analytics, planning, and S/4HANA use cases.

 

Data Stewards

ST200 | The next evolution of SAP Business Data Cloud with Dremio and SAP Reltio

Why Attend

SAP’s 2026 acquisitions of Dremio and Reltio are reshaping Business Data Cloud’s data fabric — this session gives architects and stewards the full picture on governance, master data quality, and the trusted foundation agentic AI requires — and what your organization needs to act on now.

Key Takeaways

  • Dremio’s Iceberg-native integration extends Business Data Cloud into an enterprise lakehouse — giving AI agents zero-copy access to current, authoritative SAP and non-SAP data while preserving governance.
  • SAP Reltio delivers AI-native MDM to Business Data Cloud — harmonizing trusted golden records across data domains so agents have the consistent reference layer they need to reason reliably in production.
  • Together, Dremio and Reltio close enterprise AI’s two critical gaps — unified data access without duplication, and trusted master data quality — delivering the governed foundation agentic AI demands at scale.

 

XP826 | Get a road map to your data products foundation: Powering AI outcomes

Why Attend

AI agents deliver value only when they know what data exists, where it lives, and whether it can be trusted. This session gives architects and stewards a practical road map for integrating governance, quality, and context to make enterprise data AI-ready — so agents can query the right information at scale to drive measurable outcomes.

Key Takeaways

  • Trusted data foundations require ongoing discipline — governance, quality, and semantic context at every layer so agents can discover, assess, and act with confidence.
  • Governance, quality, and context must travel with the data — keeping agents within defined trust boundaries wherever data resides.
  • Data products — governed, reusable, context-enriched units — are the building block for scaling AI outcomes, letting multiple agents consume trusted data without duplicating governance effort.

 

DA104 | Reimagining master data as the foundation for enterprise AI

Why Attend

AI agents grounded in inconsistent or ungoverned master data produce unreliable outcomes — this session reframes MDM as the strategic prerequisite for trusted AI at scale. See how SAP Business Data Cloud unifies, governs, and delivers master data as reusable products that ground analytics, autonomous applications, and AI agents in consistent, trustworthy business context.

Key Takeaways

  • Structured master data products keep agents grounded in consistent, authoritative context — eliminating the inconsistency that causes unreliable or contradictory outputs in production.
  • Data stewards now hold a critical AI risk role — the governance rules, quality thresholds, and semantic metadata they define directly determine agent accuracy and auditability.
  • Master data quality is a strategic AI enabler, not just an operational concern — organizations investing in governed master data through SAP Business Data Cloud will deploy reliable, scalable agentic AI ahead of those that do not.

 

Data Engineers

DA100 | Enhancing agentic AI with trusted business data 

DA100V | Enhancing agentic AI with trusted business data (virtual)

Why Attend

This session answers a critical enterprise AI question: how do you ensure agents access accurate, governed, and contextually rich business data? Learn how SAP Business Data Cloud’s zero-copy architecture enables AI agents to consume trusted enterprise data in place — reducing data movement while maintaining the security, compliance, and control production AI demands.

Key Takeaways

  • Zero-copy architecture gives AI agents in-place access to enterprise data — eliminating movement and duplication while keeping governance controls fully intact.
  • Data product-level governance ensures context, permissions, and semantic meaning travel with the data — making agent outputs trustworthy and auditable by design, not retrospective monitoring.
  • Together, zero-copy access and data product-level governance shift AI quality assurance from reactive to proactive — giving architects a scalable, compliance-ready foundation for deploying agents with confidence.

 

DA200 | Agentic SAP BW modernization: Your path to SAP Business Data Cloud

Why Attend

If your organization is still running SAP BW and evaluating modernization, this session delivers the most current practical guidance available — including how AI agents now accelerate the migration journey. Explore proven strategies and dedicated tools that simplify the move to SAP Business Data Cloud while maximizing the value of your existing BW investments.

Key Takeaways

  • Dedicated migration tools and AI agents now automate large portions of the SAP BW modernization journey — reducing manual effort and resource demands while maximizing existing investments.
  • Modernizing to SAP Business Data Cloud isn’t starting over — existing BW models, hierarchies, and business logic are repositioned in a governed, AI-ready data fabric as the foundation for agentic AI, analytics, and planning.
  • Moving to SAP Business Data Cloud is both a technical migration and a strategic upgrade — organizations that modernize now gain a governed, purpose-built agentic AI platform ahead of those still constrained by legacy BW.

 

CT1163 | Under the hood of the Delta Sharing protocol

Why Attend

Zero-copy data sharing is the architectural standard for AI-ready data ecosystems — this technical session gives data engineers the depth to understand and implement the open-source Delta Sharing protocol across cloud and hybrid environments. See how a Delta Sharing server delivers live Delta tables from S3-compatible storage directly to consumers like Databricks — no data movement, no duplication, and governance built in.

Key Takeaways

  • Delta Sharing delivers a zero-copy architecture — live Delta tables stream from S3-compatible storage directly to cloud consumers like Databricks with no duplication, governance and access controls intact.
  • A Delta Sharing server gives engineers practical knowledge to ingest, govern, and operationalize live data sharing between hybrid storage and cloud-native analytics and AI platforms.
  • Together, zero-copy sharing and open standards eliminate two persistent barriers — data movement and proprietary lock-in — giving engineers a replicable, vendor-neutral pattern for connecting distributed data to AI and analytics workloads at scale.

 

Data Analysts

DA105 | Enriching AI models with SAP AI Core in SAP Business Data Cloud

Why Attend

AI models are only as powerful as their business context — this deep dive shows data scientists and practitioners how SAP AI Core integrates with SAP Business Data Cloud to enable semantically enriched, enterprise-grade AI. Learn how to enhance models with rich data products from SAP Business Data Cloud, supporting benchmarking, custom AI development, agentic analytics, and production-ready applications.

Key Takeaways

  • SAP Business Data Cloud data products enrich AI models with business-specific terminology, entity relationships, and domain context — delivering accurate, enterprise-relevant outputs without the overhead of extensive custom training.
  • The session delivers a practical, end-to-end path from governed data to production AI — a clear, repeatable technical approach for agentic analytics practitioners can apply immediately.
  • SAP Business Data Cloud and SAP AI Core carry semantic richness and governance from data products directly into AI model development — closing the gap between trusted enterprise data and reliable, auditable AI outcomes at scale.

 

DA260 | Accelerate agentic planning with trusted data products (hands-on workshop)

Why Attend

The most practical TechEd 2026 session for SAP planning professionals — a 2-hour workshop where you actually build agentic planning workflows, not just hear about them. Work directly with governed data products in SAP Business Data Cloud and SAP Analytics Cloud, learning how agentic AI automates planning tasks, generates insights, and drives faster, more informed decisions.

Key Takeaways

  • SAP Business Data Cloud data products anchor agentic planning to trusted, auditable data — enabling AI agents to automate planning tasks at scale while keeping governance and accountability intact.
  • The hands-on format builds direct SAP Analytics Cloud and SAP Business Data Cloud integration experience — creating business-ready data products and configuring AI workflows that automate repeatable planning activities.
  • Participants leave with end-to-end agentic planning knowledge — from governed data product creation in SAP Business Data Cloud to AI-automated insights and decision support in SAP Analytics Cloud — ready to apply immediately.

 

DA806 | What’s next for agentic analytics and planning in SAP Business Data Cloud

DA806V | What’s next for agentic analytics and planning in SAP Business Data Cloud (virtual)

Why Attend

For SAP Analytics Cloud analysts and planning professionals, this session maps where agentic analytics is heading — what's available now and what's coming — so you can align your strategy ahead of the curve. Discover how Joule Agents are already automating insight delivery, narrative generation, and modeling tasks within SAP Business Data Cloud, transforming analytics and planning into AI-enabled decision engines.

Key Takeaways

  • Joule Agents already automate core analytics workflows — insight delivery, data modeling, and narrative generation — freeing analysts to shift from routine report production to higher-value interpretation and decision support.
  • The session's forward-looking SAP Business Data Cloud roadmap gives practitioners the context to prioritize investments, align architectures, and plan skills development ahead of the curve.
  • Together, today's live capabilities and tomorrow's roadmap give data professionals a complete picture — what to adopt now for immediate productivity gains, and what to prepare for as Joule Agents scale.

 

Data Scientists

ST103 | Behind the Autonomous Enterprise: SAP Knowledge Graph and SAP Domain Models

ST103V | Behind the Autonomous Enterprise: SAP Knowledge Graph and SAP Domain Models (virtual)

Why Attend

This session reveals the intelligence architecture behind SAP’s Autonomous Enterprise vision — showing data scientists and architects how SAP Knowledge Graph, Domain Models, and tabular AI combine to deliver enterprise AI that reasons rather than merely predict. Learn what sets SAP Business AI Platform apart: a unified foundation where enterprise context, SAP-native expertise, and predictive capabilities converge within SAP AI Core for trustworthy, explainable outcomes.

Key Takeaways

  • SAP Knowledge Graph provides enterprise context — business semantics, hierarchies, and process knowledge — enabling AI to reason about actual operations rather than produce generic statistical outputs.
  • SAP Domain Models encode SAP-specific processes, code, and metadata into immediately applicable AI capabilities, while SAP-RPT-1 delivers accurate tabular predictions without training — giving SAP organizations a significant and immediate productivity advantage.
  • Together, SAP Knowledge Graph, Domain Models, and tabular AI form a unified intelligence foundation in SAP AI Core — closing the gap between raw AI potential and trustworthy, enterprise-grade reasoning data scientists and architects can build on with confidence.

 

RA803 | SAP Knowledge Graph, AI models, and AI core power SAP Business AI Platform

Why Attend

This session connects SAP's core AI infrastructure — Knowledge Graph, Domain Models, and AI Core — giving data scientists and architects a clear picture of what's production-ready and what's on the SAP Autonomous Suite roadmap. Learn how these technologies form the intelligence foundation for Joule-embedded, context-aware enterprise applications at scale, and leave with the context to align your AI architecture decisions with SAP's direction.

Key Takeaways

  • SAP Knowledge Graph, Domain Models, and AI Core form an integrated intelligence layer — the Graph delivers enterprise context, Domain Models contribute SAP-native expertise, and AI Core provides the infrastructure to orchestrate and govern AI workloads at scale.
  • The session delivers SAP's roadmap for these technologies and their expanding role in the SAP Autonomous Suite — giving practitioners the context to understand how today's architecture choices position organizations for automated, AI-driven operations.
  • Data scientists and architects who understand this intelligence layer gain a strategic advantage — designing AI architectures aligned with SAP's direction, reducing future rework and accelerating the path to Joule-embedded enterprise applications at scale.

 

DA204 | Unlock predictive and generative AI with your data in SAP HANA Cloud

DA204V | Unlock predictive and generative AI with your data in SAP HANA Cloud (virtual)

Why Attend

SAP HANA Cloud is evolving into a multi-model AI engine — combining tabular AI, a vector engine, and a knowledge graph to power both predictive and generative AI directly on live enterprise data. Discover the latest innovations including SQL-to-LLM capabilities and deep business context for GenAI, and leave knowing how to maximize your SAP HANA investment for production-ready AI.

Key Takeaways

  • SAP HANA Cloud's tabular AI and forecasting libraries deploy predictive models directly within the database — eliminating external ML platforms and enabling faster inference on live SAP transactional and analytical data.
  • The vector and knowledge graph engines enable RAG and context-aware GenAI directly on live enterprise data via SQL-to-LLM — removing the need for separate vector store infrastructure while keeping AI grounded in authoritative SAP data.
  • Together, tabular AI, vector search, and knowledge graph capabilities within a single SAP HANA Cloud engine give data scientists a unified, production-ready infrastructure — eliminating the complexity and data movement risk of managing multiple specialized platforms.

Claim Your Ground: What 18 Days Through the American West Taught Me About Data

I just got back from 18 days on the road through the American West. Motorcycles, national parks, a trailer, and a very detailed itinerary. And before I had fully unpacked, I read Markus Kuppe's recap of DSAG 2026 and something clicked.

DSAG themed their annual conference around the American Wild West this year. "Claim Your Ground. Lead Your Business." I didn't plan the timing, but riding through South and North Dakota, Wyoming, Colorado, and Montana while the German SAP user community was leaning into that same visual language felt oddly synchronous. More than the aesthetics, though, Markus Kuppe’s reporting confirmed something I kept experiencing on the road.

A trip this complex only works if your reference data is right

The itinerary for this trip was meticulous. Eighteen days, roughly 3,500 miles, campground reservation numbers, fuel stop distances calculated per leg, specific road restrictions noted for the trailer (Teton Pass on WY-22: 10% grades, genuinely dangerous with a trailer, do not attempt). Every piece of reference data had to be correct before we left. One wrong assumption and the journey breaks.

Markus's piece from DSAG made this exact point with far more enterprise stakes. Dr. Martin Wingender from Bayer said clearly: without harmonized reference data across a diverse system landscape, aligned master data is simply not possible. Master data attributes refer to reference data. If the reference data is inconsistent across systems, your master data is inconsistent by definition. For Bayer, that means country codes, currency conversion rates, company codes, plant structures — all the structural scaffolding that everything else hangs on. Getting that wrong is the enterprise equivalent of attempting Teton Pass with a 28-foot trailer or steering the cattle in the wrong direction.

What SAP MDG and SAP Reltio look like from this angle

Markus also covered how SAP Master Data Governance (MDG) and SAP Reltio fit together, following SAP's completion of the Reltio acquisition in May 2026. The framing is worth sitting with.

SAP MDG is the authored, governed source. It knows the SAP data model deeply, produces master data that is immediately ready for SAP-driven processes, and supports the kind of workflow governance Bayer and Liebherr built their programs on. Think of it as the planned route. You set it carefully, govern changes through a defined process, and downstream systems get data they can trust.

SAP Reltio adds real-time enrichment from sources that are not under SAP MDG governance. It resolves duplicates across heterogeneous landscapes and calculates enriched records in what SAP describes as double-digit microseconds. On the road, that is the live traffic layer. Your planned route does not change, but real-time conditions inform every decision. You need both.

Inside SAP Business Data Cloud, this combination becomes the data foundation that AI agents actually need. SAP has framed it plainly: governance must shift from regulator to value accelerator. That is not a philosophical statement. It is a description of what Liebherr's "first-time-right, maintained once, used by many" MDM hub is already doing in production.

The mist is settling

Markus's central takeaway from DSAG is one I keep returning to: the AI conversation is maturing, and as the mist settles, practitioners are refocusing on the true business enablers. Clean master data is not a prerequisite to AI. It is the thing that makes AI business-relevant rather than just technically impressive.

Data practitioners have been making this case for years. DSAG 2026 was a room full of executives finally catching up.

Claim your ground.

entry.title: From Legacy to Future-Proof: Implementing SAP MDG Cloud Ready Mode and Go-live
entry.content:
Hi SAP Community

I supported this project as SAP Trusted Advisor and Focus TQM: This is what we built, and what I took away from it:

In September 2026, a leading retail group went live with SAP MDG (Cloud-Ready Mode). Not a pilot, not a proof of concept!: A full production go-live, replacing a legacy system that had reached its limits.

What made this project particularly interesting was the technology choice: the customer implemented SAP MDG in Cloud Ready Mode, the newest MDG innovation mode that bets fully on the latest SAP stack and Clean Core. The customer is among the early adopters of this Cloud Ready Mode.

The decision wasn't just about replacing software. The customer had clear requirements around data quality, compliance, and long-term maintainability. As the Head of Master Data put it  the real question was never "Does it work?"  but "Is it future-proof?". That framing shaped the entire project.

The team was a mix of customer business stakeholders, the implementation partner, and SAP. I was involved on the SAP side as Trusted Advisor and/or Solution expert. The project ran on time and without major disruptions, which (...let's be honest..) is not always a given in this space.

Key Innovations Introduced

Beyond replacing the old system, the project introduced capabilities that deliver measurable value day-to-day:

  • The Dun & Bradstreet integration stands out. Native enrichment directly in MDG means business partner data is cleaner from the start and the creation process is faster. Not a workaround, not a custom interface! -  a standard integration that works. SAP MDG enables this through the Flexible Data Provider Integration, introduced with version 2025. The required CPI mappings were handled by a dedicated CPI expert.
  • DQM derivations were another real win. Business rules automatically populate default values based on existing data, cutting down manual effort significantly. With a small enhancement on SAP BTP, the result of the derivations are visible to the requestor of the master data object as a task in his Inbox.
  • Rule-based SAP BTP workflow with a rule-based agent and flow determination to support the requirements of the customer for a flexible approval/governance process.
  • And from an architecture perspective: MDG co-deployed on the existing S/4HANA system keeps the landscape clean and reduces TCO considerably compared to a standalone setup.

Where Things Could Go Next

With Cloud Ready Mode now in place, the foundation is set for future enhancements. Possible directions include:

  • AI-powered process automation to further increase process performance and user satisfaction
  • Federated governance across a broader group structure, extending the model beyond the initial scope
  • Continuous data quality improvements building on the existing DQM and D&B foundation

What Was Achieved and What Was Learned

The project showed that master data governance is far more than a software implementation: It is also organizational development. My key findings at a glance:

  • Transparent, trustworthy business partner data as the foundation for quality and compliance
  • Improved data quality and processes: not just "get clean", but "stay clean"
  • Reduced complexity through standardization and Clean Core (direct reduction in operating costs)
  • Native D&B enrichment is a real, measurable added value
  • Centralization does not automatically solve governance: What matters is the right mix of centralization and federation 
  • "Keep it simple" - complexity is the greatest enemy of sustainable master data governance
  • MDG Cloud Ready Mode is production-ready. It's more flexible and extensible than many people think..  

The customer is very satisfied with the project and the SAP software — and has chosen to present it as a success story at the DSAG Annual Congress 2026. (see https://lnkd.in/p/eBTGCC5i)

best regards

Steffen
